How to repeat:
SET @p1 = '2023-02-03', @p2='2023-02-25';

CREATE TABLE t2 (
    created_at DATE
) 
PARTITION BY RANGE (DAYOFMONTH(created_at)) (
    PARTITION p1 VALUES LESS THAN (16), 
    PARTITION p2 VALUES LESS THAN MAXVALUE
);

INSERT INTO t2 VALUES (@p1), (@p2);

SET @s = "select * from t2 where created_at in (?, ?)";

PREPARE stmt FROM @s;

Suggested fix:
I suspect that the bug is related to to the commit: https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/commit/85008494bef26a11478370b88f83c63faee23d5b

I met the same bug in 9.0.1.

Steps to reproduce:

CREATE TABLE `customers` (
customer_id BIGINT UNSIGNED NOT NULL  PRIMARY KEY, 
customer_name VARCHAR(256), 
year_born INT, 
year_joined INT,
shard_id INT, 
KEY `index1` (`year_born`, `year_joined`)) 
PARTITION BY RANGE (`customer_id`)(
PARTITION p0 VALUES LESS THAN (5),
PARTITION p1 VALUES LESS THAN (MAXVALUE));

INSERT INTO customers VALUES (1, 'customer1', 1985, 2008, 0);
PREPARE stmt2 FROM 'DELETE FROM customers c WHERE (c.customer_id, c.customer_name) IN ((?, ?), (?, ?))';

mysql> select version();

The crash in release version is solved after picking this fix.

commit cb98e45d2fb75f67c2e65cbf8862d512e98ccce8
Author: Gabor Buella <gabor.buella@oracle.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 25 16:51:34 2022 +0100

    Bug #34801284 partitions: MySQL is trying to perform a consistent read but the read view is not assigned!
    
    Mysql crashed during evaluating IN clauses in conditions for
    partitioned tables.
    This bug was revealed by the patch for
    Bug#32311183: CPU overhead from IN lists much larger in 8.0.22.
    Which started evaluating const_for_evaluation items.
    
    This patch modifies partition pruning, to stop the evaluation
    of such items, by checking whether tables involved in the
    query are already locked. If not locked, only strictly constant
    values are evaluated.
    
    Change-Id: I93d3e4ca9b5fca23fd808c01908ea0d075cd6468
